business_problem: ETC needed an auditable, horizontally scalable backbone for tolling and smart-mobility data because rapidly growing sensor traffic made self-managed Kafka too costly, operationally risky, and hard to keep online.
solution_summary: ETC moved from self-supported Kafka to Confluent Cloud after Kafka became the central nervous system for tolling and smart-mobility systems that process sensor, device, pricing, and transaction data. Kafka already powered the company's event backbone, but rising volume—close to ten million events per day for dynamic pricing alone—made infrastructure growth, operations, and downtime risk too expensive to manage in house. On Confluent Cloud, ETC can stream roadside and traffic events into transaction-processing workflows, publish pricing to rate signs with less outage risk, and decouple event processing from downstream reporting. The managed service also absorbs capacity planning, scaling, load balancing, patching, and disaster-recovery testing that previously consumed internal staff and Amazon Elastic Compute capacity. That architecture gives ETC an auditable, scalable data platform with replayable topics and faster near-real-time analytics for customers.

evidence_quotes: A year ago, ETC was leveraging Kafka to process close to ten million events per day for its dynamic pricing solutions— a number that will likely double or triple in the next couple of years.
After conducting an internal TCO analysis, ETC decided to move from self-supporting Kafka in-house to Confluent Cloud in early 2021.

Additionally, Josh LittleSun estimated that, within a few months, the introduction of Confluent has already enabled ETC to reallocate ~50% of in-house FTE resources that had been previously dedicated to supporting open-source Kafka to more strategic projects accelerating innovation.

“Another benefit is the ability to decouple all our processing from our reporting, which allows us to process events faster and keep our database running seamlessly, while providing near-real-time analytics and quick reports to our customers.”
